decisions.reason: As a resource-intensive sports-flooring system outside the firm's main trend-led interior flooring focus, enough time has likely passed to abandon it if demand has not clearly materialized.
A mobile arena floor is costly to support and, with multiple similar sports options in the portfolio, management has a strong incentive to rationalize this weaker-fit option.
This second mobile arena floor faces the same high support burden and overlap risk, so real-options logic favors closing it if results have remained ambiguous.
Chevron parquet fits the firm's core premium, style-oriented flooring direction and is a relatively low-risk extension worth keeping on the market.
The squash court finish is niche but comparatively inexpensive to carry and still preserves upside from the firm's existing sports-floor customer base.
As a low-cost complementary accessory for sports floors, oak skirting keeps option value alive while requiring little commitment of scarce resources.
